en.html:
Kageaki"Captain."
Kanae"Ah... Mr. Kageaki... So you have come after all... for me..."
Sayo"My lady... with so much longing, and all for one person... heaven must have taken notice, no...?"
Kanae"Yes... This much at least I have been granted... to see you like this, at the very end..."
Kageaki"Captain, what is this fainthearted talk?"
Kageaki"May I sit here?"
Sayo"Please, please. You must have a cushion; I shall bring it."
Kageaki"Do not trouble yourself."
Kanae"Hehe... Surely I may be allowed to know my own body, Mr. Kageaki... Who else will know it better?... And you also, in your heart, are quite aware... are you not...?"
Kageaki"Yes..."
Sayo"My poor lady..."
Sayo"And for taking with the tea, sir... shall we settle on tempura manju...?"

en.html:
Kageaki"...Tempura?"
Kanae"For my remaining life... there is very little time left now, Mr. Kageaki............"
Kageaki"You are joking."
Sayo"Oh, it has full tradition behind it, sir. Aizu’s own specialty."
Kageaki"...So we are not dealing with a confectioner whose adventurous spirit got the better of him?"
Sayo"It is not a matter of yesterday or today, sir. The history goes back to Lord Masayuki himself, the first lord of the Aizu Matsudaira house."
Kanae"You are still allowing for a joke...? With a matter like this, would I have the heart to make one...?"
Kageaki"It is... not a joke?"
Sayo"No, no, the truth is quite genuine, sir... Only its appearance is giving the wrong impression..."
Kanae"Look at that tree in the garden, Mr. Kageaki."
Kageaki"A tree? ...That deciduous one? What about it?"
Kanae"You will agree... there is just the one leaf remaining...?"
Kageaki"Yes."
Sayo"More than three hundred years ago, in Shinshu, they say. Lord Masayuki was transferred from Takato to Aizu; the sweet came along with him—"
Kanae"...When that last leaf falls... surely I too shall die..."
Sayo"—And there you have it: exactly the same sweet is traditional in Shinshu also!"
Kageaki"Impossible—such a thing..."
Sayo"One must keep one’s eyes open in this world, sir. Even here, you see."
Kanae"Of course, from your side it is difficult to believe... But from mine... there is no such uncertainty..."
Kanae"That one frail leaf... you are looking at my very life, Mr. Kageaki............"
Kageaki"...Ah."
Kanae"————"

Kageaki"............"
Kanae"Ah... now at any moment... it may fall..."
Kageaki"May fall? But just now it actually—"
Sayo"Now, Mr. Minato. Please have one."
Kageaki"Thank you."
Kageaki"...Hmm. For taste, this has made a category of its own."
Sayo"Ho-ho-ho. No forcing yourself, sir. Take the help of the tea; for that purpose I have made it strong."
Kageaki"...No... If one gives the taste proper attention, it is rather—"
Kanae"Ah, Mr. Kageaki...! Now we have come to it... the time for parting..."
Kanae"For my last request... you will at least give me a hearing...?"
Kageaki"Captain, just now you went into the garden, put that leaf back, and came rushing in again. At lightning speed. Did you not?"
Kanae"Hehe... Now you are telling me things out of a dream..."
Sayo"Mr. Minato, even encouragement has become more than my lady can bear, please take the extra manju from here, ah, God, what has she done to deserve such treatment...!"
Kageaki"Thank you. It is only a question of getting the tongue accustomed. Quite good, actually..."
Kanae"Mr. Kageaki, please...! Before that manju... no, no, the leaf... You must hear my wish before it falls...!"

Kageaki"............"
Kanae"Ah—any moment now! My life...!"
Kanae"My life!"

Sayo"She put it back with casein glue, sir. It will take nothing less than a typhoon to disturb that arrangement."

Kageaki"Love."

Kageaki"There is none."
Kanae"GHEBAFF!!"

Kageaki"May I have another cup of tea?"
Sayo"Certainly."
Sayo"...Hm. Have I overdone the strength a little?"
Kageaki"No, it is quite all right."
Kanae"————————"

Kanae"Hah!?"
Kanae"Ah... Mr. Kageaki! For a woman in my condition... surely one last wish is not too much...!"
Sayo"So we are starting again from there itself."
Kageaki"Is there anything I can do for you, Captain?"
Kanae"There is... And for doing it, there is nobody but you... nobody..."
Kageaki"What would that be?"
Kanae"...Whatever it turns out to be... you must not laugh at me, all right...?"
Kageaki"Never."
Kanae"Dying I may be... but I am still a woman of some propriety... To go and ask a gentleman for such a thing... Ah, where am I to put my shame...?"
Sayo"My lady, you must gather courage now!"
Kanae"Yes! ...Mr. Kageaki!"
Kageaki"Yes."
Sayo"Hm. We are left with just two tempura manju. Mr. Minato, if you would be so good as to finish those also..."
Kageaki"Thank you."
Kanae"While there is still life in me...! We must not let that manju fall first...!"
Sayo"It has already fallen, my lady."
Kageaki"No, it has not."

en.html:
Kageaki"I knew it had missed the vital organs. Even so—"
Kanae"Perhaps it is being back where I was born. Not that I was pining for home all that much. Only, now I am back, I do feel that the water and air suit my body."
Kanae"The food also is very good."
Kageaki"I see. Yes, such things must count for a great deal."
Kanae"By tomorrow, I think I shall be moving as I did before."
Kageaki"That is good news. Only, do not overtax yourself. ...At any rate, I am relieved."
Kageaki"When I heard visitors were forbidden, my heart went cold."
Kanae"That was at my request. To show you a sick face and make you worry for nothing—I did not want that. But it seems my meaning did not travel properly..."
Kanae"Instead, I caused you useless worry. I am very sorry, Mr. Kageaki."
Kageaki"...No, Captain. An apology is entirely unnecessary."
Kageaki"Your injury began with my own failure. I had been thinking how many apologies I owed you. But—"
Kanae"..."
Kageaki"But—"

景明 「しかし――」
